fixes.explanation: Strikes, baker! The LORD says, “And when you strike the rock, water will come out of it for the people to drink.” (Exodus 17:6) A rock. In a desert. And water is coming out of it. I've pressed a lot of dough in my day, and not once has a rock given me a drink. The LORD also says He will stand there before Moses by the rock, so Moses isn't doing this alone.

Water, baker. The verse says it plainly: “They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.” (Exodus 17:1) A whole congregation of people, and nothing for them to drink. That's a one star review and a very short sentence.

Joshua, friend! Moses tells him, “Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites.” (Exodus 17:9) Then the very next verse says Joshua did as Moses had instructed him. (Exodus 17:10) The text gives us the order and then the doing. I wish my mornings were that tidy when I face a full batch of dough.

problems.problem: It has 6 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.
The passage does not say everyone dropped their bags or that the lack of water was the first thing they heard upon arrival.
The passage says Joshua did as Moses instructed, but it does not say he acted without arguing or pausing.
